items.title: Arturo O'Farrill interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 6, 2024
items.q: I started working with dance companies with Ballet Hispanico, Malpaso, Alvin Ailey. I just scored — I didn’t score, I was commissioned by the San Francisco Ballet Company to write a full ballet.

ctx.x: You said that before we started recording today, looking at all the boxes behind you, you said, “All I wanted to do was play the piano.”

All — that’s all I wanted to do. And I wasn’t just posing. I genuinely love this instrument. I — to this day I get up and I look at that instrument and I’m filled with emotion. That’s the privilege, the privilege of being an instrumentalist, a composer and educator. It does not fail to break my heart every day, what a beautiful and loving obligation that is that I have. Yeah. So you know I never, and it’s funny because I feel like a good, large portion of my creative life was missing until I started working with…

dance. I started working with dance companies with Ballet Hispanico, Malpaso, Alvin Ailey. I just scored — I didn’t score, I was commissioned by the San Francisco Ballet Company to write a full ballet. I just had it premiered in the ballet at the War Memorial Opera House. And I find that my work with choreographers and dancers has revolutionized the way that I play, the way that I compose, the way that I — I now understand that for me music is architectural and visual. It’s not just notes and harmony. And I have…
